newsitem.title: USA: Chase sets employee stock-option program.
newsitem.headline: Chase sets employee stock-option program.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp said on Tuesday that it would grant 450 options on Chase common stock during the next three years to each of its full-time employees worldwide.
The program, called Value Sharing, would also grant 225 options, or Value Shares, during the same time period to each of Chase's part-time employees.
Value Shares would be awarded in three equal annual installments over the next three years, the company said.
The first 150 options for full-time employees were granted Tuesday, with the remaining options to be awarded on December 16, 1997, and December 15, 1998.
The 225 Values Shares for part-time employees would be awarded on the same schedule.
The exercise price for the first tranche of options is the average of Tuesday's high and low price for Chase common stock.
Participants may exercise 100 percent of the first award when the average closing price of Chase shares during five consecutive business days equals or exceeds $110.
Chase stock was trading up 1-1/2 at 86-3/4 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
